equations_note: provenance only (QA/reviewer); the movie draws no equation labels except a plain (1) (rule G1)

equations.dot_cosine: a·b = |a||b| cos θ, Kundu §2.8 p. 52 unnumbered; on screen a plain (1) (s04, s06)
equations.shadow: |a| cos θ = a·b̂ = a·b/|b| (ours; derived on screen in s06, s07)
equations.material_derivative: Vallis §1.1.2 p. 5 (1.7) Dφ/Dt = ∂φ/∂t + (v·∇)φ, shown as v·∇φ (s13)
equations.gradient: Kundu §2.9 p. 52: ∇φ = e_i ∂φ/∂x_i (2-D here, s14, s15)
equations.local_tendency: ∂T/∂t = −v·∇T: material derivative with φ = T and DT/Dt = 0 (derived on screen in s18)
equations.matching_parts: (5x̂ + ŷ)·(x̂ + 3ŷ) = 5·1 + 1·3 = 8 with x̂·ŷ = 0, x̂·x̂ = 1 (expansion of Kundu (2.2), ours; s05a)
equations.lambert: ŝ·n̂ = cos(zenith angle), Lambert's cosine law (fluidpy.geo.terrain.insolation_factor; s20c)
equations.wind_work: power per unit area τ·u [W m⁻²] (s20d)
equations.pattern_correlation: cos θ = A·B/(|A||B|), uncentred pattern correlation (fluidpy.diag.climatology; s20e)

W2_wind_work.value: about 1 TW (10^12 W) of wind work on the oceanic general circulation, dominated by the mean zonal wind over the Southern Ocean
W2_wind_work.primary: Wunsch, C. (1998): The work done by the wind on the oceanic general circulation. J. Phys. Oceanogr., 28(11), 2332-2340. doi:10.1175/1520-0485(1998)028<2332:TWDBTW>2.0.CO;2
W2_wind_work.later: Hughes, C. W. and C. Wilson (2008): Wind work on the geostrophic ocean circulation: an observational study of the effect of small scales in the wind stress. J. Geophys. Res., 113, C02016. doi:10.1029/2007JC004371 (0.76 TW with the current-relative stress)
W2_wind_work.verified: 2026-10-28 by the motion-builder: DOIs resolved on api.crossref.org (title, authors, volume, pages); the Wunsch abstract (OpenAlex) states 'The value of about 1 TW … is dominated by the work done by the mean zonal wind in the Southern Ocean'; the Hughes & Wilson abstract gives 0.76 TW. Narration says 'about a million million watts, most of it over the Southern Ocean'.
